subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw core own named, release-tested hosting profiles, and which minimal profile/readiness contract should be accepted first?
rationale: The proposal creates permanent public configuration, health, status, probe, and release-conformance obligations that implementation review alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept the readiness foundation
options.body: Approve the condition model and default local projection first, with each additional profile requiring later acceptance and conformance evidence.

options.title: Accept all built-ins
options.body: Approve all five profiles together and commit future releases to their stable predicates, reasons, selection behavior, and upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Keep checks host-owned
options.body: Decline core profile selection and continue exposing generic runtime facts for hosting integrations or supervisors to validate externally.

recommendation.title: Accept the readiness foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the condition model and default local projection first, with each additional profile requiring later acceptance and conformance evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway HTTP ownership makes him the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether readiness topology becomes a stable core contract.
